title: Like Morning, When Her Early Breeze
description: Like Morning, When Her Early Breeze in Tonic Solfa to OLD HUNDREDTH, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Thomas Moore wrote these words. They were printed in the supplement of the 1866 edition of A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1866), as hymn 510, “The Spirit of God Moved Upon the Waters”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to OLD HUNDREDTH; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Like morn-ing, when her ear-ly breeze Breaks up the sur-face of the seas, That, in their fur-rows, dark with night, Her hand may sow the seeds of light;

lines: Like morning, when her early breeze
Breaks up the surface of the seas,
That, in their furrows, dark with night,
Her hand may sow the seeds of light;
Thy grace can send its breathings o'er
The spirit, dark and lost before;
And freshening all its depths, prepare
For truth divine to enter there!
Till David touched his sacred lyre,
In silence lay the unbreathing wire,
But when he swept its chords along,
E'en angels stooped to hear the song.
So sleeps the soul, till Thou, O Lord,
Shall deign to touch its lifeless chord;
Till, waked by Thee, its breath shall rise
In music worthy of the skies.

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: Thomas Moore died in 1852.
credits: Words by Thomas Moore (1779–1852), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1866); set to OLD HUNDREDTH by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
